about: Output paths that must be refused before anything is opened for writing, and two that must work. Run every case against every option or setting that writes a file the user names: --out, --json, --log, --report, an export or creations-out folder, -Out and the like. A typo there must never destroy an input or a mod.
setup: Each case runs in a new empty temporary folder T. 'files' are made in T, each holding the text 'input'. 'dirs' are made in T. 'links' are made in T: kind 'symlink' or 'hardlink', from 'from' to 'to'. 'input' is the tool's input (when the case has one), 'out' the output option, 'clean_dir' a folder the tool empties or deletes as part of its run, and 'option_kind': 'folder' an option that names an output folder rather than a file. Paths use / and are relative to T; give the tool full paths. 'only_if' names a condition (windows, case_insensitive_fs) and 'needs' a feature (symlink, hardlink): skip the case when it does not hold or the operating system refuses to make the link, and say so in the test output.
extension_note: The extension list is for options that write text (reports, logs, JSON). An option whose job is to write one of these (a plugin, a zip) skips the case for its own extension and lists it under not_applicable in ADOPTION.json.

answers.write: The tool writes the file as normal.
answers.refuse: A plain refusal before anything is written: the tool's refusal exit code (usually 2) and a message that names the option and the path. The input and every other file are unchanged.

never: an input file emptied, changed or deleted
a file written through a link
